newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan January bankruptcy debts up 127.9 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan January bankruptcy debts up 127.9 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Total debts held by Japanese companies which became insolvent in January rose 127.9 percent from the same month a year ago to 673.89 billion yen, Tokyo Shoko Research Ltd said on Friday.
The figure was up 12.6 percent from December, the private research firm said in a report.
The number of bankruptcies in Japan in January rose 9.5 percent year-on-year to 1,236, Tokyo Shoko said.
The number was down 3.3 percent from December, although it has exceeded 1,000 for 48 consecutive months, it said.
Of the 1,236 firms which went bust in January, 70 had debts exceeding one billion yen, Tokyo Shoko said. Of those 70 firms, eight held debts of more than 10 billion yen.

"The trend at the beginning of this year is that, in addition to companies which suffered from the (bursting of the 1980s speculative) bubble and small firms unable to cope with industrial structural reforms, medium-sized companies, which are exhausted by prolonged economy sluggishness, have also started to become insolvent," Tokyo Shoko said.
About 60 percent of bankruptcies in January resulted from factors which Tokyo Shoko said were typical in a slow economy: sluggish sales, accumulated losses and unpaid bills.
Bankruptcies increased in January in all industry sectors except for the retail and service sectors, the company said.

Companies which became insolvent in January included Kyotaru Co Ltd, a sushi restaurant chain, which was the first firm listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange to fail since mid-1993, Tokyo Shoko said.
Other failed firms included jewellery retailer Coco Yamaoka Hoshokuten and non-bank financial companies Sanwa Tatemono Sogo Finance Co Ltd and CS Sogo Service Kabushiki Kaisha, Tokyo Shoko said.
